summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator and Courtney Polk flee a desert motel after a police officer who may be corrupt comes after Courtney. The narrator hotwires a black GMC truck, zigzags through the northern desert outskirts, and switches cars to avoid pursuit. Courtney denies knowing anything about 'Pithica,' a name the narrator asks about. From a disposable phone, the narrator calls Rio about Pithica, and Rio warns him not to get involved, which he already is.
one_line: A narrator and Courtney Polk flee a dirty cop through the desert and question Rio about a mysterious organization called Pithica.
key_facts: The narrator hotwires a black GMC truck and gets its engine running in fourteen seconds.
The truck is so caked with dust and grime that it looks gray.
The narrator hopes the dirty cop has no partner nearby, since he appears to be acting alone.
Courtney Polk had been a drug mule for a cartel, which had locked her in a basement.
The narrator zigzags through the brown desert of the northern outskirts and switches cars twice in three hours.
The narrator buys a disposable cell phone at a cheap electronics store.
Courtney says she has never heard of Pithica and swears she has heard no whisper of it from her former employers.
The narrator wonders why a peace officer was on the take after Courtney Polk.
The narrator calls Rio and says, 'Pithica,' as soon as Rio answers.
Rio responds, 'Don't get involved,' and then says he can't talk.
The narrator replies, 'I'm already involved,' with his stomach sinking.
The narrator considers the cop's possible resources, including an APB or roadblocks, and decides to be impossible to find.
